candidate.answerReason: Mutual exclusivity and independence describe different properties. The retained explanation correctly restricts their incompatibility to events whose probabilities are both positive.

methods.label: Compare probabilities after one event occurs
methods.explanation: When both probabilities are positive, mutually exclusive events cannot be independent, because once one occurs, the conditional probability of the other becomes \(0\).
methods.levelReason: Uses the elementary conditional interpretation of independence and retains the necessary positive-probability condition.
